=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:29073-29157 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The five new `test_stall_judge_journal_*` tests and their helpers (`_persist_journal_body`, `_run_persist_stall_context`) are defined after `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`, so the custom script runner reports them as "unknown test name".
  WHY: CI runs this file as a script with selected test names (ci.yml:2323, :2384). In run 41049296953, orchestrate-poll shards 0, 2, 3 and 4 failed with "unknown test name", which fails the orchestrate-poll and lint jobs, and none of the new coverage runs. All reviewers that stated a severity said BLOCKER.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:29111-29137 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Four new tests (lines 29111, 29122, 29129, 29137) take the pytest-only `tmp_path` parameter, but the custom runner at line 26593 calls `func()` with no arguments.
  WHY: Even after the tests move above the `__main__` guard, each raises "TypeError: missing 1 required positional argument: 'tmp_path'". The file convention is `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` (around line 27023, and test_custom_runner_tests_need_no_pytest_arguments). Severity disagreement: sonnet BLOCKER, luna BLOCKER (finding combined with the guard placement), glm MAJOR; the highest is used.
- tests/test_attempt_journal.py:(whole module) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The new 347-line test module is not wired into any CI step and is not listed in UNWIRED_ALLOWLIST.
  WHY: static-checks fails at tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py:60 (run 41049296953), which fails the lint job, and the helper's tests never run. ci.yml is outside the files_touched grant, so the fix needs a recorded justification or is blocked on scope. Severity BLOCKER.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:2081-2105 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `if:` of the "Record attempt journal entry (clarify)" step (line 2085) lacks `steps.clarify_route.outputs.skip_codex != 'true'`, which post_clear (line 2046) and post_questions both require. On skip_codex routes both steps are skipped, so the outcome logic (lines 2092-2100) records `outcome=fail`.
  WHY: Every fast-path clarify run (orchestrator-managed, closed or automated-release issues) writes a false "clarify | fail" entry that the stall judge, the unblock judge and later stages read as a real failed attempt. sonnet adds that parse_codex.blocked runs are also recorded as fail, and glm adds that the `blocked != 'true'` check is missing too. Severity MAJOR from all reviewers that stated one.
- scripts/attempt_journal.py:346-360 (_gh(); gemini cites 425-438) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: _gh() silently falls back to a direct `gh api` call when `import gh_api_retry` fails, and no staging list ships gh_api_retry.py next to attempt_journal.py. It is absent from REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS (scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh:57, 93-100) and from the fetched_scripts lists (clarify.yml:484, plan.yml:591, implement.yml:1475, orchestrate_poll.yml:615).
  WHY: Every staged runtime bypasses the shared rate-limit breaker and retry policy that the docstring and the agents.d fragment promise, so writes continue under rate limiting and transient errors drop journal entries. Severity MAJOR from all reviewers that stated one.
- tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py:537-600 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The four new `test_attempt_journal_*` contract tests are defined after `if __name__ == "__main__": run_all_contract_tests()`, which walks globals() before they are bound.
  WHY: A standalone `python3` run skips the four P1 contract tests without any error. Disagreement on CI impact: sonnet says CI runs the file through pytest (ci.yml:2602), so CI does run them; gemini says ci.yml:2602 runs it as a standalone script, so they never run. Severity disagreement: sonnet NIT, glm MAJOR; the highest is used.
- scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:704 (also scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1316-1319, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh, scripts/attempt_journal.py resolve_target()) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The review writers pass `--head-ref "${HEAD_REF:-${PR_HEAD_REF:-${GITHUB_HEAD_REF:-}}}"`, but in the codex-agent job on dispatched rounds all three sources are empty and `LINKED_ISSUES_JSON` is unset. HEAD_REF is step-local at review_autofix.yml:2950, PR_HEAD_REF exists only in the deterministic-skip job (line 1114), and LINKED_ISSUES_JSON is exported only at line 4308. resolve_target() therefore falls through to the PR number.
  WHY: Later review and resolver rounds write a second journal comment on the PR instead of appending to the issue's journal, which breaks the "one comment with four entries" done-when and hides those rounds from the judges. sonnet explicitly checked and dropped this claim: scripts/review_collect_pr_metadata.sh:271 exports LINKED_ISSUE_FALLBACK_NUMBERS_JSON at review_autofix.yml:2776, so resolve_target() picks the issue when the PR body has a closing reference. Severity MAJOR from glm; gemini and minimax stated none.
- scripts/attempt_journal.py:110-115, 132-167, 226-233, 320-330 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The entry limits set no aggregate comment-size bound. Forty entries, each with up to twenty 300-character file paths and ten 300-character deletion paths, are all serialized by build_comment.
  WHY: The machine record can exceed the 65,536-byte comment limit used by plan.yml:2744-2746. GitHub then rejects the PATCH/POST and later appends keep retrying the oversized record, so the journal stops advancing. Severity MAJOR.
- (CI check-runs / pre-push gate; not mapped to a line) | severity=high | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PR's pre-push gate lists `ruff` and `shellcheck` as failures caused by this change, on scripts/attempt_journal.py, the new test code and the five edited shell scripts. sonnet also notes that tests-promote-stall-and-review and tests-release-and-log-analysis failed, with truncated logs.
  WHY: static-checks and lint stay red until these are fixed. sonnet confirmed that all module-level names used by the new test code exist, so the claim that names are missing is false. Severity disagreement: sonnet NIT, glm MAJOR; the highest is used.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml, clarify.yml, plan.yml:"Record attempt journal entry" steps (2084-2101 in clarify, 2759-2782 in plan, 6314-6343 in implement) | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Every writer step is `continue-on-error: true` and gated only by `PERSIST_JOURNAL_ENABLED` (default `false`). There is no per-stage kill switch, no opt-out label, no documented behaviour for SKIP_PLAN/SKIP_IMPLEMENT, and no rate limit or circuit breaker on the writer path.
  WHY: With the switch on, every stage issues journal reads and writes with no per-repo cap, no audit log and no way to turn off a single stage, which contradicts the docstring's claim that writes are bounded. The reviewer stated no severity; medium is a ledger default.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Pair workflow/script changes with the contract tests the plan calls for (this repo guards workflow behaviour with focused contract tests)." / "The P1 deliverables and tests listed in the plan are implemented and pass."
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/ci.yml, a pytest step for tests/test_attempt_journal.py next to the existing pre-push gate tests (ci.yml:655-656); also tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py, where the stall-judge journal tests must sit above main() and take no arguments
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: tests/test_attempt_journal.py is referenced by no `.github/workflows/*.yml` file, and tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py::test_every_test_file_runs_in_a_workflow (tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py:57-62) failed in CI run 41049296953 / head 38bfec0 naming this file, which fails static-checks and lint. The five stall-judge tests never run because of the `__main__` placement (sonnet). Scope disagreement: sonnet and minimax say ci.yml is outside the files_touched grant, so this must be escalated; glm says the grant lists `tests/**`.
- requirement: P1 entry schema — "`failure_key`: the first 12 hex of `workflow_failure_heal.fingerprint(<workflow>, <step>, error_signature(<failure text>))`, else `""`"
  expected_change_site: implement.yml "Record attempt journal entry (implement)", `_resolver_attempt_journal_append` in scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh, and the clarify/plan record steps
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/attempt_journal.py supports `--failure-workflow/--failure-step/--failure-text-file` (build_parser at lines 583-585) and computes a key only when they are given (attempt_journal.py:528-533), but no caller passes them, so every entry, including outcome=fail, has failure_key "".
- requirement: "Done when: with the switch on, a fixture issue run through plan, implement and two review rounds has one journal comment with 4 entries." / "The linked issue is found from the ai/issue-N head, or via LINKED_ISSUE_NUMBERS logic."
  expected_change_site: issue-target resolution in the review writers (scripts/review_commit_changes.sh, scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh, scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh via resolve_target())
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: test_done_when_plan_implement_and_two_review_rounds_give_one_comment_with_four_entries passes `--issue 5` explicitly, while the production review writers pass only `--pr`/`--head-ref`. The head-ref sources are empty on dispatched rounds: review_autofix.yml:2950 assigns HEAD_REF only inside the checkout step and does not export it, and GITHUB_HEAD_REF is empty on workflow_dispatch. resolve_target() therefore falls back to the PR number, and later rounds create a second journal comment on the PR.
- requirement: P1 plan: "with the variable off, the PR must be production-safe and change no existing behaviour" / "every prompt, judge context and stall-judge cache key is byte-identical to before"
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh invoke_stall_judge (lines 19626-19644 and 19659-19670) and the cache-key construction
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The off case is correct. With the variable set, `_persist_journal_key` is appended after `${_judge_recent_comments_hash}` (line 19666), which changes the cache key, so pre-P1 decision-cache entries become unreachable. This on-case reset is undocumented.
